question: Does the frozen discovery inspection order expose recurring local structures across whole-image communities, beyond visiting more family IDs?
hypothesis: At 50 photos the existing discovery order covers more r2 families in at least two global communities than the existing global-centroid order.
design: Post-hoc descriptive analysis of frozen orders; no refitting, model extraction, threshold search or new policy selection.
primary_metric: Number of families observed in at least two distinct frozen global communities among the first 50 selected photos.
secondary: cross-community families with at least two selected parents in each of two communities
coverage among families whose full-census median partition Jaccard is at least 0.5
family-level counts, semantic ratings and examples retained separately
scope: All 2899 photos eligible for the existing region catalog. Automatic memberships measure structural coverage, not validated semantic identity. Census semantic ratings are correlated agent adjudications, not independent targets.
compute: Light CPU only; cached catalog and existing selected-photo orders; no cloud cost.
